messages:
incident-bot: paging sre_oncall for SEV2 — elevated gateway 502/504 rates from inference-gateway in prod-us-west-2. automated alert: 3m > 5% 5xx across ~1200 rps. runbooks: vpc-egress-failure.

sre_oncall: I’m on it. hitting the dashboards now. any customer-facing pages?

jess_prod: saw spike at 11:03UTC, a few customers reported increased latency/timeouts on embeddings endpoints. some 504s from gw-infer-prod-{1,2,3}.

raj.kapoor: grabbing logs. early signals show many upstream connection resets: `connect() failed (111: connection refused)` and `upstream timed out (110: Connection timed out)`.

maria: running quick healthcheck on NAT/peering — nothing in console obvious, but conntrack counts are high on transit-appliances.

alex.t: copying tcpdump from gw-infer-prod-3: ```
12:34:56.789 IP gw-infer-prod-3 > registry.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com: Flags [S], seq 0, win 65535, options [mss 1460], length 0
12:34:56.800 IP registry.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com > gw-infer-prod-3: Flags [R], seq 0, win 0, length 0
```

sre_oncall: interesting. R from S3 side could be SNAT port collisions causing packets to appear from unexpected ports. last-time we saw similar was ephemeral port depletion. but metrics show ports free.

netops-bot: route-change event 11:01UTC — transit-peering appliance config applied: `asymmetric-snat-fix-v2` (author: infra-ops).

raj.kapoor: that lines up. config change applied 2m before spike. possibility: appliance is rewriting source ports in a non-idempotent way -> SNAT collisions and upstream RSTs.

maria: can we test by forcing a single instance to use alternate egress NAT?

alex.t: doing `sudo ip route add default via 10.20.0.1 dev eth0 table 200` and `ip rule add fwmark 0x1 lookup 200` then marking test traffic. spinning small canary traffic to model-registry.

jess_prod: customer-impact update: several PLG customers see 10–20% error rate on inference calls, some timed out requests retried into errors. CS notified C-suite for a few enterprise accounts.

sre_oncall: quick mitigation plan: 1) reroute inference-gateway egress for one AZ to alternate NAT that does not pass through transit-peering 2) increase conntrack timeout/size on transit appliances 3) rollback peering config if confirmed root cause. who can do NAT swap?

maria: I can swap AZ-B pool to nat-egress-standby. initiating: `asg attach-instance --instance-id i-0abc... --target-group nat-egress-standby` (abbrev).

raj.kapoor: while that’s happening i'm increasing conntrack: `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=2000000` and `sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=300`. applying to transit-appliances.

netops-bot: nat-egress-standby now serving AZ-B (started at 11:11:23UTC). healthchecks green.

alex.t: canary traffic to registry via standby NAT shows success: no RSTs, complete GETs for artifacts.

jess_prod: error rate dropped from 7.2% to 1.1% for AZ-B flows. global error rate down to ~3.4%. customers still impacted in other AZs.

sre_oncall: good. continue migrating AZs in rolling fashion. disable peering route on one transit node and test before mass rollback.

maria: migrating AZ-C now. will do one at a time, ~2–3m each.

customer-success: heads-up — pushing high-level status update to affected customers: saying we’ve identified a networking peering config change causing intermittent timeouts, we’re rerouting traffic and will follow up with RCA.

raj.kapoor: logs on transit-appliance show SNAT table reported overlapping port ranges post-change. excerpt: `SNAT pool overlap detected: [1024-61000] collides with dynamic rewrite mapping`.

sre_oncall: can we confirm the appliance change? who approved `asymmetric-snat-fix-v2`?

netops-bot: change authored by infra-ops@redwood, change-id ch-9923, applied 11:01UTC.

alex.t: recreating the change in staging — I can reproduce RSTs when appliance rewrites ephemeral ports into same outbound range for concurrent flows. reproduction steps in staging: apply config, run parallel curl 1000x -> connection failures appear.

jess_prod: operations update: all AZs migrated to standby NAT, error rates back to baseline (<=0.5%). CS sent interim note.

sre_oncall: mitigation complete. next steps: 1) revert `asymmetric-snat-fix-v2` on transit nodes (netops to coordinate), 2) run post-change validation suite, 3) schedule follow-up postmortem with infra-ops, netops, runtime, and cs reps, 4) consider implementing automated canary for peering config.

maria: rolling rollback now (staggered). will keep one transit node in read-only for debugging.

netops-bot: rollback started 11:22UTC, rollback complete 11:26UTC on all transit-appliances.

raj.kapoor: running recovery verification: `curl -I https://registry.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/weights/abc` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK` from gw-infer-prod-1. conntrack levels back to baseline.

jess_prod: closing customer loop: CS to send RCA summary in 2 hours. incidents channel to be updated with postmortem doc link.

sre_oncall: handoff to daytime oncall @maria for follow-ups and RCA. leaving notes: root cause suspected SNAT rewrite collision introduced in peering config ch-9923; mitigation was full egress reroute to standby NAT and rollback of change. watchlist: conntrack thresholds and transient errors during peering changes.

maria: ack, will take it. will open follow-up ticket INC-2026-047-RCA and add timeline + logs.

customer-success: thanks — we’ve already sent affected customers a concise update. will coordinate postmortem distribution. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident INC-2026-047 marked RESOLVED -> mitigation succeeded, customer impact limited to transient errors, follow-up RCA scheduled.
